title: Heterogeneous kernel coalescence surge — mitigation playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a mixed-quantization release we observed a ~3x p95 token latency spike across certain models when the scheduler coalesced requests onto heterogeneous kernel sets. This ticket captures a pragmatic mitigation playbook (fast rollback paths, emergency kernel pinning, and throttled probe windows) and a set of follow-ups to avoid recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy mixed-quant model variants (fp16 + int8) in a single node pool with default scheduler probing enabled
2) Generate synthetic burst workload with variable sequence lengths to trigger dynamic kernel paths (use benchmark harness: benchmarks/mixed_quant_burst_v2)
3) Observe scheduler logs for repeated kernel probing and coalescence decisions (logs: scheduler/probe.log), correlate with KV cache miss rate and batch composition
4) Measure p50/p95/p99 token latencies using tracing: console -> model -> traces -> 2026-02-17 10:00-11:00
5) Confirm increased eviction and slow paths by inspecting runtime metrics: runtime.kernel_swap, runtime.kv_cache_miss, runtime.batch_compaction_rate
root_cause_summary: A scheduler heuristic that aggressively coalesces compatible requests into mixed-execution batches failed to account for cross-kernel cache residency and quantization-induced divergent kernel runtimes. When the scheduler grouped int8 and fp16 requests onto the same execution path, intermittent kernel handoffs caused cache thrashing and probe amplification, amplifying tail latency under bursty loads.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix 1: Temporarily disable mixed-quant coalescing in the scheduler (flags: scheduler.enable_mixed_quant_coalesce=false) — rolled out to 3 regions
Hotfix 2: Introduce emergency kernel pinning rule that forces homogeneous kernel selection per batch when KV cache residency drops below threshold (runtime.flag: kernel.pinning_threshold=0.6)
Hotfix 3: Short-circuit the probe window expansion logic to fixed 30s backoff for suspect model families (scheduler.probe_backoff_ms override)
Rollback path: Automated canary rollback triggers if p95 increases >40% for 5 minutes after a config change; playbook documented in runbook/runtime-hotfix-rollback.md
long_term_actions: 1) Rework coalescing heuristic to account for KV cache affinity and per-kernel median runtime; add offline model traces to train heuristic
2) Add continuous canaries that exercise mixed-quant paths under synthetic bursts and fail the rollout if kernel_swap_rate > 0.05
3) Implement per-model kernel affinity heatmaps in Console (visualization + alerting) to make coalescing decisions observable to SREs and PMs
4) Reduce probe amplification by adding jitter and conservative exponential backoff tied to capacity stress signals
5) Extend runtime metrics with 'kernel_warmth' percentile to measure practical cache residency rather than naive hit-rate
follow_up_notes: 2026-02-18: Incident detected by synthetic canary alerts, alerted on Slack #infra-incidents — rotation lead: Ravi Patel
